requirements.title: CRITICAL mutual exclusion and segment ordering are ensured across images
requirements.definition: The processor shall ensure that once an image has commenced executing the CRITICAL block, no other image commences executing it until that image completes execution of the construct. The image shall not execute an image control statement during the block. The sequence of executed statements is a segment. If one image completes without failing and another is next, the first image's segment precedes the second; if the first completes by failing, its previous segment precedes the next image's segment.

review_rationale: batch112: independent fresh-context source review against pinned J3/24-007 (sha256 7371e889...), plus a closeout re-verification. The authoring prompt wrongly guessed these sections were IF and CASE; the author read the pinned PDF, found they are actually CHANGE TEAM and CRITICAL, and registered what the source says. The reviewer independently verified the titles as Purpose and form of the CHANGE TEAM construct, Execution of a CHANGE TEAM construct, and CRITICAL construct, and recorded the override as correct behaviour. The reviewer read all 39 base units in the original PDF, verified 39 base / 75 fine units, 33 requirements and 85 facets (all pending), and confirmed the accounting claim that only 21 base units are newly accounted, with the claimed asymmetry of twelve numbered items in 11.1.5.1, none in 11.1.5.2 and six in 11.1.6 independently checked. Both permissions were accepted: the 11.1.5.2 p3 and 11.1.6 p5 sentences of the form it is permissible to branch to an end statement only from within its construct carry a permission and, through the word only, a paired restriction boundary, and the packet captures both halves. The dominant risk in this scope is image-execution observability, and it produced one blocking finding, C11TR-001, which was closed by a correction commit and re-verified. The 11.1.5.2 p5 requirement that all active images of the new team execute the same CHANGE TEAM statement had been filed as a diagnostic rejection; it is in fact a dynamic multi-image synchronization obligation on the program, which a conforming processor is not required to diagnose and generally cannot, and for which no portable executable oracle exists in this suite's single-image observational regime, since observing divergence would require exactly the timing, scheduling and interleaving evidence this project forbids. The requirement remains registered; only its unsupportable plan was removed, its diagnostic obligation is now not-required, and the facet is recorded as unimplementable source-control evidence. The author then swept the whole packet against the same test and produced a 22-row table classifying every facet as implementable, unimplementable-context-dependent, or source-control only, reclassifying substantially more than the one facet found, including the successful-change-team synchronization, post-change and post-END segment delays, cross-image segment precedence, the CRITICAL one-image-at-a-time and mutual-exclusion facets, and the failed-image material. The reviewer audited that table against the source, checking specifically for over-suppression, since an unobservability claim that is too broad is itself a defect in this project, and examined the team-restoration rows and the CRITICAL segment classification for local observability; no over-suppression was found, no facet is missing from the table, and no facet could pass vacuously in a single-image run. Final decision: accept, no blocking findings. This registers source accounting only: it is not fixture approval, it supplies no execution, and it approves no oracle.
